PullRequest.Title: sessions: Add an External section and session import action
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- Add a non-empty External section above Done in workspace and time grouping, while preserving pinned sessions and custom groups.
- Introduce `sessions.list.groupExternalSessions`, enabled by default and controllable by automatic experiments. It changes grouping only; the existing external-session visibility preference still controls which sessions appear.
- Suppress New actions in that section, retain Mark as Done, and reuse the existing None/Recent/Last 24 Hours/Last 7 Days/Last 30 Days visibility menu. The section and filter use distinct icons.
- Add a capability-gated Import action immediately before Archive/Mark as Done, with context-menu and multi-selection support. Import adopts the existing session in place without sending a message, using the adoption machinery from the preceding PR.
- Keep grouping, drag-and-drop, workspace labels, accessible help, and row actions consistent when external status changes.

Import restores the existing session before adopting it, so it may hydrate/resume provider SDK state; it does not submit a prompt or create a duplicate session.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client` passes with the complete stack checked out.
- Focused discovery, adoption, Import protocol/provider/management, grouping, menu, accessibility, and comparison tests: **240 passing** with `--force-device-scale-factor=1`.
- Changed-file ESLint, `npm run valid-layers-check`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- All **7 External section fixtures** render without errors.

An existing comparison connector test expects a 1px computed stroke and fails at this machine's system display scale. The identical failure was reproduced on unchanged `main`; the focused suite passes at explicit 100% scale. No unrelated comparison styling was changed.

## Stack

**3 of 3**, based on #337559 (`benibenj/agents/external-session-adoption`).

1. #337558 — repository-independent external discovery
2. #337559 — automatic adoption and immediate client updates
3. This PR — External section and explicit Import action

Merge in this order.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call and cold restore call graph are explicit, including provider materialization, full-message retrieval, database reads, and state retention. The exact-session metadata API already exists, so avoiding full hydration is bounded and does not require a shadow catalog. Provider-specific duration and typical transcript size affect severity, not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Provider SDK chat materialization, full transcript reads/hydration, session-database reads, and retained turn objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For a cold session the cost grows with its transcript and persisted session state; the new multi-selection action invokes this path once per selected external session at effective concurrency 1, so completion latency grows roughly with the sum of all selected sessions' restore times.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Import is blocked on unrelated provider and history hydration, causing avoidable action latency, I/O/CPU work, and memory/GC pressure; importing more than the 10-session residency limit can additionally restore and then immediately release earlier sessions.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, an unopened external session stayed as list metadata until the user actually opened or messaged it; no provider chat was materialized and no transcript was loaded merely to change ownership.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new import request always awaits restoreSession before changing the registry ownership bit, even though Import neither opens the session nor sends a message. On a cold session restoreSession proceeds through exact metadata lookup, materializeChat, session-database hydration, provider getMessages for the full default-chat transcript, and retention in AgentHostStateManager.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line `await this.restoreSession(session);` places full provider/session hydration on every Import request before the added registry adoption call; this work did not exist for unopened external sessions before the PR.
Findings.Title: Avoid restoring full sessions just to import them
Findings.Impact: Selecting Import on an unopened session can take as long as opening and hydrating that session; multi-selecting N external sessions serializes N such cold restores before the action reports completion.
Findings.Evidence: AgentService.restoreSession only short-circuits when AgentHostStateManager already contains the session. Otherwise _restoreSessionState calls agent.getChatMetadata, agent.materializeChat, opens persisted metadata, calls provider.chats.getMessages, hydrates/interleaves every turn, and stores the resulting summary/turns. The provider already exposes the exact-session getChatMetadata path used by _registeredSessionMetadata, and AgentSessionRegistry.adoptExternalSession itself only needs the registered identity and a database write. The UI action at sessionsViewActions.ts:966-967 loops selected sessions with await, making the cold cost cumulative.
Findings.Recommendation: Validate the registered external session with the existing exact-session metadata lookup, adopt it in AgentSessionRegistry, and publish/update the surfaced summary without materializing the chat or loading turns. Keep restoreSession only for sessions that are actually opened; preserve the not-found check by rejecting when the exact metadata lookup confirms the provider session is gone.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render, regroup, filter, and interact with the new External sessions section
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The visible list synchronously filters/sorts existing session objects, partitions external sessions in the same grouping pass, builds section children, and updates row context keys. Configuration changes and external-status changes trigger the existing list update path; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work is on this rendering critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of already-visible sessions S. The added partition and external predicates are O(S); the pre-existing sort remains O(S log S). Virtualized row rendering bounds DOM work to rendered rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI thread; updates are synchronous and no added async fan-out occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session adapters and observables are reused. The grouping setting is read from configuration; no new cache or retained-key collection is introduced. External identity changes invalidate the list once through the existing observer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the added list work is linear in the same collection already sorted and grouped.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large session lists can still make any full regroup visible, but the diff adds only constant-time predicates per session and no evidence establishes a material regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; the section is computed in the existing full-list pass and adds no expensive boundary or unbounded state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Import one or multiple unopened external sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action awaits each selected session in sequence. Each call crosses renderer-to-Agent-Host RPC, and a cold host session then must complete metadata lookup, provider chat materialization, persisted-state reads, full default-chat transcript retrieval/hydration, registry adoption, and the response before the next selected item starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send vscode/importSession and await its response
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per selected eligible session; no batching, effective concurrency 1.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No explicit Import request existed; unopened external sessions incurred no RPC merely to change ownership.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each response is awaited before the next selected session and before completion status is announced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve exact provider metadata, materialize the default chat, and fetch the full provider transcript
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For each cold selected session: one metadata lookup, one materialization, and one full getMessages retrieval; warm resident sessions skip these calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider materialization and history retrieval occurred when the session was actually opened/restored, not for a standalone ownership change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All provider work blocks that session's import response and therefore the serial multi-import action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read session metadata, chat backing, annotations, workspace transitions, and related persisted state during restore
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Multiple bounded persisted-state reads per cold imported session, with transcript-associated allocation scaling by history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unopened external sessions remained list metadata and did not hydrate their session databases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required by restoreSession before registry adoption returns, despite Import not opening the chat.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and rewrite the AgentSessionRegistry ownership entry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one registry read and, while external, one registration write per imported session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same adoption write occurred only on the first accepted outgoing user message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the ownership operation Import actually needs and is expected on its critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N selected sessions after filtering to external, import-capable, unarchived targets, plus each session's transcript size H_i. Effective cost is approximately the sum of N cold restore costs and all H_i; warm resident sessions skip most restore work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Exactly one import at a time because sessionsViewActions.ts awaits inside a for-of loop. Provider work within one restore has limited internal parallelism, but different selected sessions do not overlap. Residency reconciliation is sequenced and retains at most 10 ordinary sessions by default.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm AgentHostStateManager entries make restoreSession short-circuit after residency handling. Cold sessions materialize and retain full state; after the 10-session residency limit, earlier imports may be released while later ones restore. In-flight coalescing is per session and does not coalesce distinct selected sessions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high confidence from the direct changed call to restoreSession and the traced cold restore path through materializeChat, persisted-state reads, getMessages, turn hydration, and state retention.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider materialization time and transcript sizes vary, but cold restores demonstrably perform heavyweight work and multi-selection makes latency cumulative.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity eager-work regression. Import should validate through the existing exact metadata path and publish the ownership update without hydrating conversation state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Propagate imported ownership to the sessions list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentSessionRegistry fires adoption synchronously; because Import first restored the session, AgentHostStateManager metadata is updated immediately. A catalog reconciliation is queued asynchronously and is not awaited by importSession.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recompute current session metadata from registry/catalog and republish surfaced summaries
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Usually one coalesced pass per adoption burst, potentially more when serial imports are spaced by cold restores; each pass scales with the visible catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same reconciliation mechanism ran after message-triggered adoption; explicit Import adds another adoption trigger but preserves coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Queued off the Import response critical path; immediate metadata comes from the restored state.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of adoption events and total catalog size. The reconciler coalesces events arriving while a pass is in flight into at most one trailing pass, though serial long-running imports can allow separate passes to complete between items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single promise chain serializes reconciliations; storm-driven requests are coalesced to one active plus one dirty trailing run.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: listSessions coalesces same-mode in-flight computations and provider metadata can use prewarming/bulk reads. Registry epoch invalidation prevents stale reuse.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the coalescing and off-critical-path behavior; lower confidence in repeated-pass cardinality, so it was not reported separately.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether multi-import causes one or several completed reconciliation passes depends on provider restore duration versus catalog-pass duration.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding. Coalescing bounds bursts, and the dominant actionable regression is the unnecessary cold restore already reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open accessibility help and External section/context menus
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Localized help strings are assembled on explicit help invocation, and menus are resolved when headers or rows request actions. These paths perform configuration/context-key reads only.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant-sized help and menu entries; row menu work applies to the invoked row or section.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI work with no asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses existing menu/configuration services; no new long-lived collection or cache key is created.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed call sites.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 35 changed files and both pages of the sessions-list diff. Reported one eager-work regression: Import restores and hydrates a cold session before flipping ownership, and multi-select serializes that cost. External section grouping otherwise adds linear in-memory partitioning and reactive row metadata without new expensive boundaries or unbounded retention.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
